## 1a: mean function without NA handling

```{r}
v = c(1:50, NA, 55)
vector_mean <- function( df){
  tot = 0
  for ( element in df){
    tot = tot + element
  }
  return( tot / length(df))
}

vector_mean( v)

```

# 1b: mean with NA handled
```{r}
super_vector_mean <- function( vector , na.rm = F ){
  tot = 0
  for (element in vector){
    if( is.na(element)){
      if(na.rm){
        next
      }else{
        return( NA)
      }
    }
    tot = tot +element
  }
   n = sum( !is.na(vector))
  return( tot / n) 
}

super_vector_mean(v , na.rm = T)

mean( v , na.rm =F)

```
##### My loop base function for "mean" are expected to agree because I included lines that handle presence of NA values within passed vector during iteration. The final sample size is also calculated by first turning the  NAs into  logicals ( TRUE/FALSE) then summing , which adds all the TRUEs(1s) to produce actual sample size since the FALSEs will be 0s.

# 1c: accessing data from DuckDB repository

```{r}
library(repoquet)
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)

config_path <- "repoquet_public_example/repository_config.R"
cfg <- load_repository_config( config_path)
temp_dir <- file.path(cfg$FormattedDBPath, "duckdb_temp")
dir.create(temp_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

con <- open_duckdb(
  FormattedDBPath = cfg$FormattedDBPath,
  DBName = cfg$DBName,
  TempDirPath = temp_dir,
  GB = cfg$DuckDB_GB,
  ReadOnly = TRUE
)


nhanes_tables<- DBI::dbListTables(con)
nhanes_tables <- sort(grep("^NHANES_" , nhanes_tables, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE))
head(nhanes_tables, 5)



nhanes_table <- nhanes_tables[32]
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, paste0("DESCRIBE ", nhanes_table))


bmi_data <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, paste0( "SELECT * FROM ", DBI::dbQuoteIdentifier(con, nhanes_table)))

head(bmi_data)
str(bmi_data)

#column to calculate mean from 
weight_in_kg <- bmi_data$BMXWT
super_vector_mean( weight_in_kg , na.rm = T)
#regular mean function
mean( weight_in_kg , na.rm = T)


```

# 1d:  Testing for correlation between the BMXBMI vs BMXWAIST

Ho: correlation between body mass index and waist circumference = 0
Ha: correlation between body mass index and waist circumference != 0


```{r}
body_mass_index <- bmi_data $BMXBMI
waist_circum <- bmi_data $ BMXWAIST

cor.test( body_mass_index , waist_circum)


```
From the cor.test results;
there's a positive correlation ( r =0.9311994 ) between body mass index and waist circumference.
As BMI increases, waist circumference also increases.
t = 827.9 and p-value < 2.2e-16 suggest there's evidence for the alternative hypothesis. This shows relationship does not imply causation, but rather suggest it's worth investigating further.
